Student-led coalition begins push for sweeping institutional reforms in Serbia

01 Nov 2026, 10:38 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.bbc.com

2 min read

Key takeaways

Post-Election Transition

Following the victory of a student-led movement in recent Serbian elections, the newly elected MPs have publicly called for the immediate resignation of key figures within the nation's security, intelligence, and judicial sectors. The movement, which successfully unseated the Serbian Progressive Party of former president Aleksandar Vučić, seeks to address concerns regarding institutional corruption.

Core Objectives of the Student List

Newly elected members of parliament, a diverse group including academics, medical professionals, and economists, are operating under a comprehensive 1,200-page manifesto. Key pillars of their reform agenda include:

  • Institutional Accountability: Demanding the dismissal of police and intelligence officials allegedly involved in past legal violations.
  • Media Reform: Pursuing the liberation of the media landscape, starting with management changes at the state broadcaster, RTS.
  • Anti-Corruption Measures: Implementing a 'lustration' law to bar public officials found to have violated citizens' rights.
  • Economic Policy: Reclaiming misappropriated state funds and increasing investment in education.

Challenges and Criticisms

While supporters view these steps as a necessary 'spring cleaning' of the government, the transition faces significant obstacles. Acting President Ana Brnabić has characterized the moves as 'revolutionary justice' rather than the rule of law, expressing concerns over the potential targeting of media outlets. Analysts, including those from the European Policy Centre, note that because the previous administration held broad control over the state apparatus, dismantling these entrenched structures will be a complex, time-consuming process. Additionally, the new government must navigate Serbia's delicate foreign policy, maintaining a balance between European Union integration and existing ties with Russia and China.

Verification

This transition remains ongoing as the official handover of power is expected to span several weeks. Interested parties can monitor official updates through the Serbian parliament's portal and verify policy progress against the published Student Plan manifesto. Official statements from both the incoming administration and the opposition party are being documented via local state news and international news bureaus reporting on the region.
